lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.unitTitle: PF1 — Earning Income: Compensation Packages and Career Pathways
lessonRef.title: Concept model B: pathway cost: certificate, apprenticeship, or degree

focus: pathway cost: certificate, apprenticeship, or degree
objective: Compute the full cost of three fictional pathways including earnings given up, and find how long each takes to repay against a stated baseline.
scenario: A fictional school-leaver could work now at $32,000 a year or take one of three invented pathways. Every cost, duration, and wage below is fictional.
safetyNotes: Every figure, person, employer, institution, offer, account, and document on this task sheet is fictional and exists only for practice.
No real transaction is part of this lesson, and no real bank, card, brokerage, tax, or login detail is ever requested. If a task sheet ever appears to ask for one, stop and tell a trusted adult.
This lesson teaches general financial concepts and does not advise anyone about their own money. For a real decision, talk with a trusted adult or a qualified licensed professional.
materials: the fictional pathway table in these directions

tasks.directions: The baseline is working now at $32,000 a year. Pathway A, a certificate: 14 months, tuition $9,400, earning $12,000 a year during it, then $44,000. Pathway B, an apprenticeship: 36 months, no tuition, earning $28,000 a year during it, then $58,000. Pathway C, a degree: 48 months, tuition $46,000, earning $8,000 a year during it, then $67,000.

prompts.text: What earnings does Pathway A give up against the baseline over its 14 months?
What is Pathway A’s full cost, tuition plus forgone earnings?
What is Pathway C’s full cost?

tasks.directions: Now find how long the higher wage takes to repay each pathway’s full cost, measured against the $32,000 baseline.

prompts.text: How many years does Pathway A take to repay its cost? Round to two decimal places.
How many years does Pathway B take to repay its cost? Round to two decimal places.
How many years does Pathway C take to repay its cost? Round to two decimal places.
Pathway B repays fastest and Pathway C ends at the highest wage. Explain why the payback figures do not settle the choice on their own, and name what a 20-year view would add.

remediation: If Pathway B appears to cost nothing, note that it still gives up $4,000 a year against the baseline for three years. Zero tuition is not zero cost when the alternative pays more during the same period.
extension: Compute total earnings over 20 years from the start of each pathway, counting the during-pathway years at their stated wages, and say whether the ranking changes.
